messages.subject: Demand a composite overall score
parts:
Dear Phil:

　　A research of mine harvest each domain score of a 6-dimentional model (for eldly health scale) using mirt.  We now demand a composite(overall) score, have mirt offered such function?

　　And if I need to applying "maximum information method" to obtain this overall score, could you please enlighten me how to do it？ I've only learned using R (mirt and plink) in IRT field.

　　Thank you very much.

　　Best wishes

Allen 　　


maximum information method: Simply speaking, compute a direction α on which vector θ have maximum information. In this case the overall score can have smallest estimation error.

Refer: Yao, L. (2010). Reporting valid and reliable overall scores and domain scores. Journal of Educational Measurement, 47(3), 339–360.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Demand a composite overall score
parts:
If you are interested in a overall (general) composite score then you really should be constructing a model to capture this information. The bifactor model (supported by mirt) is one such candidate, and likely answers your question well. Yao's "maximum composite information" criteria is somewhat ad-hoc compared to directly modelling a composite, which the higher-order and bifactor models are intended to do, so I'd recommend going with those routes. HTH.

Phil
